name: Stoicism
overview: Scripture presents a call to radical self-denial and commitment to Christ that surpasses even the most austere practices seen in Stoicism. John the Baptist's austere lifestyle of wearing camel's hair and subsisting on locusts and wild honey, along with his abstention from normal eating and drinking, illustrates a form of disciplined living (Matthew 3:4; 11:18). Yet Jesus demands more than mere external discipline, teaching that true discipleship requires taking up one's cross and subordinating natural affections, loving Him above all family ties (Matthew 10:37-39; 16:24). This aligns with Paul's teaching that the mind and body are in conflict and must be brought under Christ-centered submission, highlighting that self-denial is not stoic endurance but a transformative obedience to Christ's lordship.
